overview: In the Signature teaching of metal casting basics, Sand-cast method is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. core_concepts: Lost-wax: burning out a wax model for detailed bronze and silver
Pouring: smooth steady pours without turbulence
key_laws: Dry everything: moisture in a mold or crucible causes steam explosions.

vocabulary: Draft: the taper letting patterns leave the sand
Annealing: softening a casting with controlled heat
methods: Sand-cast method: ram sand around the pattern in the flask, remove pattern, cut sprue and riser, pour, cool, break out

overview: In the Signature teaching of metal casting basics, Current Research Frontiers in Metal Casting Basics is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Pattern means the model the mold is formed around, slightly oversized for shrinkage Safety means foundry work demands full protective gear and dry molds Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Advanced material that follows.
core_concepts: Pattern: the model the mold is formed around, slightly oversized for shrinkage
Safety: foundry work demands full protective gear and dry molds
key_laws: Dry everything: moisture in a mold or crucible causes steam explosions.
Full protective gear, every pour, no exceptions.
vocabulary: Sprue: the channel metal flows through into the mold
Parting line: where the two mold halves meet
methods: Sand-cast method: ram sand around the pattern in the flask, remove pattern, cut sprue and riser, pour, cool, break out
history: Casting is 6,000 years old, from bronze-age axes to art bronzes; backyard foundries revived the craft with online knowledge-sharing in the 2000s.
